samples.summary: Harness board mount omits `suppressSlideChrome: true`, so several editor paths call the newly-refused store methods and throw uncaught
samples.evidence: The board mount calls `S.initializeEditor({ canvas, overlay, store, hostWidth, hostHeight, dpr, viewport })` with a store wrapped by `asBoardStore` (34 methods now throw `"…" is not supported on a board`), but it does NOT pass `suppressSlideChrome: true` — the flag production's board mount passes for exactly this reason (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:288`, and `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:310-318`: "Without this flag, right-clicking the empty board canvas and picking 'Change layout…' throws uncaught"). Concretely reachable, unguarded paths in the harness: `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:529` (Cmd+M → `store.addSlide` → refused), `:556` (Cmd+Shift+D → `store.duplicateSlide` → refused), `:383-384` (Cmd+D with nothing selected → `store.duplicateSlide` → refused), and `packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:3421-3427` (right-click empty canvas → "Change layout…" → `store.applyLayout` → refused). Each throws out of a keyboard/menu handler, i.e. an uncaught exception the persona's `crash` oracle will record as a product defect that does not exist in the real board. Worse for state: `MemSlidesStore.batch` pushes an undo snapshot BEFORE running the callback (`packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:1789-1793`), so the throw leaves `board.canUndo` reporting `true` after an action that changed nothing — a second manufactured violation. Before this change the refusals did not exist, so `asBoardStore` is what makes these paths crash.

samples.summary: A target-less `scroll` action cannot pan the harness board — the wheel listener is bound to the canvas, and the tool wheels at the current mouse position (0,0 at session start)
samples.evidence: `canvas.addEventListener("wheel", onWheel, { passive: false })` is the ONLY thing that pans the harness board. The driver executes `scroll` as `await page.mouse.wheel(dx, dy)` and only moves the pointer first when the action carries a `target` (`packages/frontend/scripts/hunt-ui-runner.mjs:326-333`). At session start the pointer is at (0,0) — the canvas is centred (`margin: 0 auto`) below the header+toolbar, so its rect starts around x≈320,y≈83 — hence a bare `scroll dy 900` dispatches the wheel outside the canvas and the listener never fires: the viewport does not move. The new charter states the opposite as measured fact (`scripts/agent/charters-ui/board-author.md`: "A plain `scroll` PANS. Measured: `scroll dy 900` moves the viewport to `panY: -900`"), so a persona predicting `board.viewport` changed across a scroll gets a `violated` verdict and can file a false major ("scrolling does not pan the board"). Note the verifier script itself works around this by moving the mouse onto `board.elementCenter("card")` before `page.mouse.wheel` (`packages/frontend/scripts/verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:846-853`), so the oracle lane never exercises the path the persona will take. Production binds the wheel handler to the whole `container`, not the canvas (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:610`).

samples.summary: Grid snap is exposed as "real" to the persona but is not wired to the editor — `getSnapGrid` is never passed, so toggling snap changes no drag outcome
samples.evidence: The board `initializeEditor(...)` call passes no `getSnapGrid` (production passes `getSnapGrid: () => gridSnapRef.current ? gridStep(vp.current.zoom) : null`, `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:302-303`) and nothing calls `applyGridBackground`. `gridKind`/`gridSnap` are React state consumed only by the toolbar. Yet the new charter tells the persona the snap is live and load-bearing for drag predictions: "THERE ARE TWO SNAPS, AND ONE IS A TOGGLE… On top of that the toolbar has a GRID SNAP, off in this harness by default and switchable from `Grid`. Both move a drag away from where you aimed… drag somewhere well clear, or predict the snapped value" and "THE GRID CONTROLS ARE REAL" (`scripts/agent/charters-ui/board-author.md`), plus personas.json's `content-and-undo` brief ("The `Grid` menu and its snap checkbox are REAL state here"). A persona that enables snap and predicts the snapped landing point gets `violated` on a harness-only gap and can file a false "snap to grid does nothing" defect.

samples.summary: Board mount starts no render loop, unlike production's per-frame `editor.render()`
samples.evidence: Production's board drives `editor.render()` from a RAF loop (`packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:715-720`) so asynchronous work (font/image loads, deferred metrics) repaints; the harness board relies solely on the editor's own `markDirty`/`render` calls after interactions. The slides branch of the same file has the same omission, so this may be intentional, but on the board the viewport can change without any store change (`setViewport` → `markDirty` → `render` is the only repaint) and any async asset resolution after that will never be painted — readers that measure DOM handles (`board.handleCenter`) could then report positions from a stale overlay.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. page.tsx:537-545 mounts the board editor with a store wrapped by asBoardStore but passes no suppressSlideChrome (grep finds zero occurrences anywhere under packages/frontend/src/app/harness), while production's board mount passes suppressSlideChrome: true at board-view.tsx:288. The option's own doc (editor.ts:310-318) says omitting it makes 'Change layout…' throw uncaught, and editor.ts:3421-3427 pushes that menu item precisely when the flag is falsy. The flag flows to the key rules at editor.ts:1536, so the guards at keyboard.ts:383-384 (Cmd+D, empty selection), :529 (Cmd+M) and :556 (Cmd+Shift+D) are all skipped, and the following lines call store.duplicateSlide/addSlide — names listed in BOARD_UNSUPPORTED (mem-board-store.ts:29,31,35) whose proxy (mem-board-store.ts:76-82) unconditionally throws. runKeyRules (keymap.ts:70-80) has no try/catch and editor.ts:2727-2728 fires it via `void`, so the error escapes as an unhandled rejection. Additionally memory.ts:1789-1793 pushes the undo snapshot and clears redoStack before invoking the callback, so the throw leaves canUndo() true after a no-op. No upstream guard makes any of this unreachable; real missing-guard crash plus a broken undo invariant, squarely in the correctness lane.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is verifiable in the repo. The harness binds its only wheel listener to the board canvas (page.tsx:571; a grep over src/app/harness finds no other wheel or window listener). The runner executes a target-less `scroll` as a bare `page.mouse.wheel(dx, dy)` with no preceding pointer move (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:326-333), so the event is dispatched at Playwright's default (0,0). Geometry confirms (0,0) is off the canvas: the context viewport is 1600x1200 (hunt-ui-runner.mjs:365) while the board wrap is 960x540 with `margin: 0 auto` (page.tsx:508-513), sitting below a header with px-4 py-2 padding (page.tsx:691) and the board toolbar (page.tsx:743), putting the canvas rect at roughly x>=320, y>0. A target-less scroll is a legal action: target is described as "optionally for scroll" in the tool schema (hunt-ui-tool.mjs:602), with dx/dy at 611-612. Meanwhile the charter states the opposite as measured fact ("A plain `scroll` PANS. Measured: `scroll dy 900` moves the viewport to `panY: -900`", board-author.md:65, with a dependent claim at :69), and the oracle sidesteps the path by moving the mouse to board.elementCenter("card") before wheeling (verify-hunt-oracles.mjs:847-853), so the passing oracle never covers it. No guard, fallback binding, or schema requirement makes the unguarded path unreachable. This is a real behavioral/logic defect in the correctness lane: documented, oracle-blessed behavior is unachievable on the path personas are told to take, producing false "violated" verdicts and spurious defect reports.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The harness board mount at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:537-545 calls S.initializeEditor with only {canvas, overlay, store, hostWidth, hostHeight, dpr, viewport} — no getSnapGrid — whereas production supplies it at packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-view.tsx:302-303. In the engine, packages/slides/src/view/editor/editor.ts:6352-6357 derives the grid step solely from this.options.getSnapGrid?.() ?? null, so with the option absent grid quantization is permanently off and toggling the checkbox cannot change any drag or resize outcome. The harness's gridKind/gridSnap state (hunt/page.tsx:400-401) is consumed only as BoardToolbar props (hunt/page.tsx:749-752); a repo-wide grep shows applyGridBackground is called only from board-view.tsx:355,369,764, never from the harness, so the grid mode is likewise inert there. Meanwhile scripts/agent/charters-ui/board-author.md:79-83 and 94-95 tell the persona the grid snap "move[s] a drag away from where you aimed" and to "predict the snapped value", and personas.json:62 repeats that instruction. The path is reachable (checkbox rendered and wired to setGridSnap), nothing guards it, and the result is a wrong-behavior/false-violation gap — a real logic-wiring defect in the correctness lane, not style, tests, or architecture.
